title: Madd laazim: the six-count madd: rule card and examples
subject: Qur'an & Tajweed
unit: Summer 1: Al-Baqarah 285 to 286; madd laazim and 'aarid
source: Written for quran/y4 lesson 34 (Pupil PDF worksheet: Madd laazim rule card and examples)
intro: Lesson 34. Read the rule and say every example aloud. Point to each word in your mushaf. Then answer the questions.

panels.title: Madd laazim
points: A madd letter followed by a fixed sukoon or shaddah
Always six counts, joined or stopping

blocks.title: Sort into: Laazim: always 6 / 'Aarid: 2, 4 or 6 at a stop
blocks.task: sort them into the columns: Laazim: always 6, 'Aarid: 2, 4 or 6 at a stop.
blocks.answer: Laazim: always 6: ٱلضَّآلِّينَ; ضَآلًّۭا. 'Aarid: 2, 4 or 6 at a stop: نَسْتَعِينُ (stopping); ٱلْمَصِيرُ (stopping)

keywords.def: lengthening a sound by a set number of counts

questions.q: Read «وَلَا ٱلضَّآلِّينَ» (1:7) with six counts on the madd.
Pupil PDF: sort ten madd examples into laazim, 'aarid, muttasil and munfasil. Today's rota group recites Al-Fajr 25 to 30.
questions.a: Each example placed with its count.

questions.q: Extend: find the madd laazim in Ad-Duha.
Stretch: why is «ٱلضَّآلِّينَ» never shortened even when joined?
questions.a: The shaddah is fixed in the word; laazim does not depend on stopping.
A) six counts. Alif followed by a shaddah: madd laazim, six counts.

questions.q: Madd laazim needs a madd letter followed by ...
options: a hamza in the next word

questions.q: Think again: 'Aarid can be 2, 4 or 6 counts. Why do you think laazim is always 6?
questions.a: Laazim means 'necessary': the sukoon or shaddah after it is fixed, whether we stop or not, so its length is fixed too.
